title: Ife artists model terracotta figures
summary: At Ife, artists made terracotta figures and vessels depicting people, animals and spiritual beings, in styles ranging from naturalistic to abstract.

citations.locator: Essay title and paragraphs on form, excavation context and ritual reuse
citations.note: Supports the linked claims within the stated date and attribution limits.

claims.text: At Ife, artists made terracotta figures and vessels depicting people, animals and spiritual beings, in styles ranging from naturalistic to abstract.
The Met groups this tradition around 1000–1400 CE; these are approximate cultural boundaries, not dates for every surviving sculpture.
Many finds come from secondary settings. Ritual reuse complicates attempts to reconstruct their original functions; these works cannot all be identified as royal portraits.

review.corroboration: The Met essay was inspected. Its excavation caveat is retained; independent corroboration of the chronology was not established.
